chunks: The daughters are hasanat (good deeds/blessings), and the sons are ni'mah (a bounty). For indeed, one is rewarded for the hasanat, but one is questioned about the ni'mah.

key_terms.حَسَنَاتٌ: Plural of hasanah: meritorious deeds or blessings for which one earns divine reward
key_terms.نِعْمَةٌ: Ni'mah: a divine bounty or gift, for which one will be asked to account on the Day of Judgment (Quran 102:8)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about daughters versus sons in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reframes the social valuation of daughters and sons using Quranic terminology: daughters are like hasanat (meritorious deeds) for which a person receives divine reward, while sons are like ni'mah (bounties/blessings) for which a person will be held accountable before God on the Day of Judgment. This teaching inverts the pre-Islamic Arab bias that favored sons, elevating daughters to a status that brings direct spiritual benefit to parents.
